messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for tenant 'acme-analytics' on us-west-2 region. Current window 10m: p95=450ms p99=2.3s error-rate=0.8% — paging oncall @olivia

olivia (oncall): on it. acked the page. pulling traces and recent deploys.

samir: I see a small spike starting ~1711998000, correlates with sustained concurrency from that tenant. spikes when stream chunks are enabled.

jess: can you paste the latency heatmap? I'm seeing streaming stalls reported in telemetry.

samir: attaching quick snippet from trace aggregator:

```
trace_id: 0x7e9f..a3
span: model.infer.kv_cache (duration=1.9s)\nspan: http.stream.chunk (duration=1.5s)\nspan: scheduler.queue (p99=600ms)\n```

mike: interesting — scheduler queue p99 at 600ms plus model.kv_cache 1.9s explains tail. looks like KV cache misses for long context prompts.

carla (customer-rep): customer reported degraded UX in channel earlier — they said long pauses during streaming for long transcripts. they submitted an example prompt: extremely long concatenated instructions (~120k chars).

olivia (oncall): that aligns. acme runs single-tenant high-concurrency jobs with long prompt histories. we might be hitting an execution path that doesn't use chunked KV well.

sean: checking node-level metrics for the dedicated pool assigned to acme-analytics. CPU and GPU utilization are moderate, but memory pressure on GPU worker process is high and we see occasional OOM reclaims.

jess: mitigation plan: 1) throttle concurrency for that tenant to reduce queuing, 2) temporarily disable streaming chunk coalescing, 3) route tenant to fallback smaller-context model variant to avoid huge KV hits.

mike: I can push a temporary routing rule. propose: route new requests from tenant -> model-x-small-context for 15m, and set concurrency cap 6 per-tenant.

olivia (oncall): do it. set an alert to auto-revert after 15m unless manual ack. also notify customer.

deploy-bot: /apply-route-rule --tenant acme-analytics --route model-x-small-context --duration 15m --note "emergency tail-latency mitigation"

deploy-bot: Route rule applied (change_id=chg-20260314-1).

samir: applied per-tenant concurrency cap via rate-limiter: limit=6 burst=2.

incidents-bot: ACTION: mitigation in place. monitoring for next 10m. pre-mit p95=450ms p99=2.3s.

(8m later)

jess: post-mit window: p95=380ms p99=720ms error-rate=0.3% — major improvement on tail but still above SLO for some customers.

carla (customer-rep): Acme acknowledges faster responses but still sees occasional >1s pauses on long transcripts. they're willing to accept temporary degradation if we can provide root cause.

sean: dug into the worker logs. When prompt size > 60k chars, we see repeated KV cache evictions causing repeated recomputation. stack: tokenizer -> chunking -> cache-miss -> recompute.

samir: that's consistent with a corner case where tokenizer inserts many special tokens causing effective sequence length to blow up and the runtime to switch to slow path. we haven't optimized that path for single-tenant high-concurrency bursts.

olivia (oncall): immediate next steps for RCA: - collect a reproducible prompt example from customer (carla) - instrument KV cache hit/miss per request - capture a full worker core dump if OOM reclaims persist

carla (customer-rep): uploaded example prompt to secure share: https://internal-files/acme/long_prompt_2026-03-14.txt (shared with eng-privacy).

mike: starting an instrumented run on a replica with that prompt (non-prod). adding log lines for cache-hit/fill.

jess: also schedule a canary rollout of a kernel patch that changes eviction policy (LRU -> size-aware). do it in non-prod first.

(20m later)

mike: instrumented run shows: 1) prompt tokenized to 175k tokens after special token expansion, 2) KV cache chunking produced ~90 pieces, each chunk causing frequent host->device transfers due to misaligned chunk sizes.

samir: so the effective overhead is not pure compute but transfer and scheduler thrash under high concurrency. That explains why GPU utilization looked moderate but tail latency high.

olivia (oncall): for customer-facing update: we throttled concurrency and temporarily routed to smaller-context model which improved tail. we're still investigating root cause and will propose a permanent fix (routing options, improved eviction, or model-side truncation). ETA for full RCA: 24-48 hours.

carla (customer-rep): Acme wants to know whether we can prioritize a dedicated fix — they run revenue-impacting jobs. they'd like timeline and option for a short-term SLA credit if this continues.

jess: escalate to PMs and account team. I'll open a tracking ticket and tag infra/priority-high.

sean: ops note: schedule a maintenance window to test size-aware eviction kernel in dedicated pool tomorrow 03/15 02:00-04:00 UTC. will notify customer if we run it on their pool.

olivia (oncall): handoff: I'm still assigned oncall for next 30m then switching to samir for next shift. Samir please monitor metrics and be ready to rollback route rule if any regressions.

samir: ack. I'll take over at 1712003000 and watch p99, scheduler-queue, and worker GPU memory trends.

incidents-bot: NOTE: Handoff registered: from olivia to samir at 1712003000. All active mitigation artifacts: chg-20260314-1, rate-limit-id rl-7321.

(2h later, follow-up)

samir: follow-up notes: after size-aware eviction patch test in non-prod, p99 for long-prompt workload dropped to ~420ms on test cluster. no regressions observed. planning staged rollout next week.

jess: created RFC for model-side truncation + runtime size-aware eviction. links: https://rfd/internal/eviction-v2. priority: P1.

carla (customer-rep): Acme accepted temporary mitigation and requested weekly updates until fix is in prod.

olivia (oncall): closing thread for now — ongoing work tracked in RFC and ticket INF-4852. reopen or ping #incidents if p99 exceeds 1.5s for acme-analytics again. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> monitoring. closed by olivia at 1712004578
